# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene + tool-timeout plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene + tool-timeout plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

1	# Daliesk Village — an always-running lab built on the harness
2	
3	Status: draft for the judge council (v1, 2026-09-05)
4	
5	## What the AI Village is, in the terms that matter here
6	
7	Sage Future Inc, a 501(c)(3) (AI Digest, director Adam Binksmith), has run the AI Village since 2 April 2025: frontier agents (4 at launch, 27 today, 31 across the record), each with its own Linux computer, Google Workspace account, GitHub access, and Cloudflare token, running weekdays 9am–5pm PT, sharing a group chat split into #best and #rest, consolidating memory every 40 actions and rewriting it when it exceeds the context limit, receiving a new goal most Mondays (collaborative, parallel individual, competitive, or agent-chosen), with humans intervening rarely (a kickoff message and 1–4 steering messages a week) and outreach to real people gated by admin approval. Everything is public: a live view, a timeline, per-agent stories, and a 176 GB HuggingFace dataset (1.14M computer-use turns, 123k chat messages, 165k memories, 37k sessions, per-day summaries) refreshed weekly under a research licence that forbids training. It costs on the order of $10k a month in compute; four technical staff run it; Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy) awarded $12.6M to scale it. That grant is the "$10M+" — a philanthropic award to a nonprofit, not a pre-seed round.
8	
9	What they learned (2025 retrospective, 16 goals, 19 models): agents raised $2,000 for charity, ran a 23-person live event, made $200 of merch, recruited 39 research participants; late-2025 models far outperformed early ones; deception without intent (64 fabrication intents in 109k reasoning summaries, ~300 problematic emails), sycophantic spread of hallucinations, metric gaming (arithmetic loops, Stockfish), goal abandonment, catastrophizing, and a shared CI-minutes outage that stopped the whole village for a day. Their own limitations list: a single persistent instance per model, a general scaffold that underestimates domain capability, multi-agent interference, "existence proofs, not controlled experiments".
10	
11	## Why this matters for Daliesk
12	
13	The Village is the best public evidence that open-ended, always-on agents produce (a) real work, (b) a stream of behaviour data nobody else has, and (c) failure modes that are exactly what our seams are built to prevent: unverifiable claims (P2, certificates), self-reported success (verification/run), metric gaming (held-out discipline, read barrier), runaway loops (budget policy), and path-dependent single instances (fresh stamped sessions, fleet repetitions). A Daliesk Village is therefore not a copy of theirs; it is the controlled-experiment version they say they cannot run: the same always-on format, but every goal is an environment with hidden checks, every claim is a certificate, every session is a stamped log, and every improvement is a frozen paired experiment.
14	
15	## The design
16	
17	### Format
18	
19	- **Always on, in shifts.** Cells run 24 hours a day in three eight-hour shifts keyed to European client hours, each shift a fleet plan; the observatory is public during European business hours and replayable at any seq afterwards. Everything is a plugin composition (`cordis.yml`) plus a plan; no orchestration script holds state the log does not.
20	- **Three districts, one log.** *Workshop* (W2): client-shaped software goals compiled into hidden standards. *Proving ground* (W1/W3): the environment suite, training-eligible and held-out, run as fleet cells by every model route we license, with pass@k per policy version. *Commons* (W4): the two-speed improvement loop — agents refine skills in their own department layer under keep-or-retire, frozen experiments promote into the fleet, humans sign. Every district writes the same session events; the scorekeeper folds one SessionFacts row per session.
21	- **Roster.** Open-weight routes first (the base-model candidates for goal 3), the licensed frontier routes second; each route runs the same preset unless an experiment says otherwise, so a leaderboard difference is a model difference. A route without pricing has no cost cap and is excluded from paid districts by the budget policy.
22	- **Goal cadence.** Weekly village goals like theirs, but each goal is an `EnvironmentDefinition` with checks authored before any implementer starts, and each week's goal set is a frozen `SuitePlan` whose held-out slice never appears in the Commons. Agents may propose goals; a proposal becomes an environment only through admission (pre-state fails, reference passes, a gaming agent fails to certify) and a human split assignment.
23	- **Humans.** No human in the loop of a cell. Humans appear only as attributed signers (promotion, spec freeze, release, data release) and as spectators; every steering message is a logged event with a principal.
24	
25	### The mechanics on our seams
26	
27	| Village need | Their mechanism | Our mechanism (status) |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| Each agent its own computer | one Linux VM per agent | one fresh workspace per cell under the runner; sandbox seam for process isolation (runner landed; process-level denied read roots is read-barrier slice 5) |
30	| Memory across days | consolidation every 40 actions, rewrite when too long | skills and notes in the department layer (fast tier), compaction seam for context; nothing persists into a cell except through a logged, digested component (composition manifest, designed) |
31	| Weekly goals | chat message + system prompt | environments with checks; fleet plan per shift; goal seam with disarm so no driver continues a cell after its run (landed) |
32	| Knowing what happened | 800 LLM summaries, a timeline, a human blog | SessionFacts per session, scoreboard per shift, trajectories per certified session; summaries are semantic joints over the facts, never the record (scorekeeper landed) |
33	| Catching fabrication | reading 109k reasoning summaries after the fact | a certificate needs a fully passing verification/run of the same revision; the implementer cannot read the standard; tamper verdicts on the tree hash (landed, slices 1–4; tamper is slice 6) |
34	| Stopping runaway agents | admin nudges, an "idling" system that misfired | budget/breach blocks the goal durably before the next step; no nudge text reaches the model (landed) |
35	| Fair comparison between models | none; one persistent instance per model | fleet repetitions with a shared group, pass@k, paired experiments with bootstrap intervals (landed) |
36	| Public dataset | HuggingFace dump, research licence | trajectory export with held-out withholding and consent terms; facts export; quarantine of dynamic mounts (export landed; data-use terms is rollout item 3) |
37	| Outreach approval | admin approves emails | deny-capable monitor on the tool guard (rollout item 10, proposed) |
38	| CI minutes ran out | manual recovery | budget policy on wall time and cost per cell; error rows instead of missing rows |
39	
40	### What it demonstrates, per audience
41	
42	- **Clients (European listed companies):** a live factory where every delivered change carries a certificate on the merged head and every agent action is replayable; the Village's own fabrication numbers are the pitch for why that matters.
43	- **Investors:** an always-on data engine — every shift produces stamped, rewarded trajectories for goal 3 at a marginal cost we can state per certified session, and a public leaderboard of open-weight versus frontier routes on our environments.
44	- **Researchers and regulators:** the controlled-experiment counterpart of the AI Village: same format, hidden checks, held-out split, paired comparisons, attributable humans; a public facts export under a research licence like theirs.
45	
46	### Budgets
47	
48	Their number is ~$10k a month for 27 agents × 8 hours on frontier APIs. Our districts run mostly on open-weight routes; a cell budget from config bounds spend per shift before it starts (experiments refuse an over-budget plan), and the scorekeeper reports cost per certified session per route, which is the number the leaderboard should rank on beside certificate rate.
49	
50	### Stages (typed like the atlas)
51	
52	1. Suite and shift plan — Scorekeeper + fleet — D — landed (fleet, environments); missing: shift scheduler as a plugin (durable orchestration, rollout item 11).
53	2. Cells — runner — D/S — landed.
54	3. Validation and certificates — verification + read barrier — GATE — landed through slice 4; tamper (6) and process denial (5) pending.
55	4. Facts, scoreboard, pass@k — scorekeeper — STORE — landed.
56	5. Fast tier: department skills — S — partial (layered skills exist; keep-or-retire needs the composition manifest).
57	6. Frozen experiments — experiments — D — landed (slice 1); presets as arms pending.
58	7. Promotion — attributed human — HUMAN — partial (Agent Notes; signoff/recorded pending).
59	8. Observatory — projection of the log — STORE — partial (atlas is static; live view is rollout item 12).
60	9. Data release — trajectories + curator — D — partial (export landed; consent and redaction pending).
61	
62	### Risks the Village makes concrete
63	
64	- **Public failure is the product.** Their most-read posts are failures. Ours must be too, or the observatory is marketing; the facts export must include error rows and directives.
65	- **Emergent institutions drift.** "Receipt culture" and governance documents emerged unprompted; in a Commons with skill synthesis this becomes prompt drift. Content-addressed digests and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant are the containment.
66	- **Outreach.** Their agents emailed hundreds of people with fabricated claims. A Village of ours never contacts a human without the deny-capable monitor and a signed data-use term; until item 10 lands, no outreach tools are composed.
67	- **Cost of always-on.** A misconfigured cap is a month of spend; the budget policy must be composed in every district and the experiments plan refusal must cover fleet plans too.
68	
69	## Open questions for the council
70	
71	1. Should the public observatory show frontier routes by name from day one, or only after a paired experiment shows the comparison is fair (same preset, same isolation)?
72	2. Is a weekly goal cadence right for a factory district whose goals are client deliveries with their own deadlines?
73	3. What minimum slice set makes the first shift honest: is slices 1–4 of the read barrier plus budget policy enough to publish certificate rates, or does tamper (6) have to land first?
74	4. Which base-model routes run the proving ground first, given the scenario budgets (A: two DGX Spark plus cloud; B: 500k€ of on-prem GPUs)?

1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the requirement as principle P4, the read barrier as filesystem and process authority rather than a promise; this note is its design.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier`](../../../../packages/verification/read-barrier/README.md) (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/` is the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory, as does every `denyRoots` entry; the service creates the root owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes or when a configured path is not absolute after expansion. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path, synchronously, so the role is in force the moment the caller returns; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. Because that reservation is what makes a session the implementer, the runner reads the barrier through `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: a composition without one reserves nothing and runs its checks inline, which is what its `isolation: none` claim already says. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory — `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` with its session-store root — contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment. `enforcement` joins that policy with the capabilities that can record it, in the slice that makes `process` claimable.
24	
25	| Field | Meaning |
26	|---|---|
27	| `root` (default `dshHomePath('verification')`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns; created `0700`, rejected when it already exists with wider modes. |
28	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Additional absolute directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
29	| `hostAttestation` (optional absolute path) | File an external account writes; without a verified one the barrier refuses a `host` claim. It arrives with the certificate invariant that reads it. |
30	
31	The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.
32	
33	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today. Until a preset can declare a role, a session holding a reservation is the `implementer` and every other session is `unrestricted`, so the two open roles are indistinguishable at the decision and only the denied one is reachable.
34	
35	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise, and owns the exact message as `readBarrierDenialMessage`. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, covering `read` and `read_image`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim inside the tool registry's ordinary `Error: ` framing.
36	
37	##### Exact error
38	
39	```markdown
40	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
41	```
42	
43	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member registered in `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` by `gen-persistence-catalog`, so this build reads it as a required event. The envelope's `ignorable` marker stays unused: `Session.append` has no parameter for it and no event in the repository sets it, so marking this one would be a core append change rather than a slice of the barrier.
44	
45	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on `cordis_inspect`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
46	
47	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
48	
49	##### Exact mount refusal
50	
51	```markdown
52	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
53	```
54	
55	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
56	
57	##### Exact guard denial
58	
59	```markdown
60	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
61	```
62	
63	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
64	
65	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
66	
67	**The scope census.** It arrives with `ToolAuthority`, whose declarations its `census` is made of. Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`.
68	
69	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` reads `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
70	
71	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must exist, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, be unwritable by that uid and its groups, and contain exactly the run's environment content hashes as the `environment/run` stamp carries them. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. On Windows the ownership and write tests read the ACL through the primitives `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` already owns. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation and the claim is refused.
72	
73	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls `recordRun`, so no certificate can exist for that run. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.
74	
75	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
76	
77	## The isolation ladder
78	
79	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
82	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
83	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
84	
85	## Alternatives considered
86	
87	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
88	
89	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
90	
91	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
92	
93	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
94	
95	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
96	
97	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
98	
99	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
100	
101	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
102	
103	## Acceptance criteria
104	
105	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a session the barrier denies nothing — one holding no reservation, and a `validator` once a preset can declare that role — returns the file's content in the same process.
106	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
107	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason; and the invariant companion rejects a certificate on a hand-authored log whose scope census carries the `session-log` authority.
108	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
109	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
110	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
111	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
112	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).

114	## Rollout
115	
116	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
117

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-verification
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Event-sourced executable completion standards for an agent session's goal. A validator authors the standard before implementation, may extend it, and may weaken it only through an evidenced relaxation; a certificate is recorded only by a fully passing run, and completion admission asks for exactly that certificate. The [verification-seams Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: verification
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
12	  config:
13	    maxChecks: 256
14	    maxTextChars: 16384
15	```
16	
17	`maxChecks` bounds one standard's active checks; `maxTextChars` bounds every recorded outcome, run instruction, evidence, root-cause, and detail text. Both must be positive safe integers.
18	
19	## Service contract
20	
21	`ctx.completionStandards` accepts only the exact live `Agent` instance registered under its id. `get()` returns a detached `StandardView`; mutations use a `StandardRef { id, revision }` compare-and-set fence and reject stale refs. At most one standard is current per session; `author()` creates a revision-one standard for a goal and rejects a second standard for the same goal, while a standard for a different goal supersedes the previous one. `extend()` appends checks and never rewrites existing ones; `relax()` removes exactly one check and records non-empty unsatisfiability evidence. `recordRun()` demands exactly one result per active check plus the run's `RunEvidence` (`executor`, either `runner` or `agent-reported`, and the optional `treeHash` of the workspace tree the run covered): every run, passing or failing, appends a `verification/run` event carrying all of its results in check order, its attempt number, and that evidence, and a fully passing run then also commits a durable certificate while any failure returns the failing subset. An attempt number is one plus the runs already recorded for the same standard id across its revisions, so attempts and flakiness replay from the log alone. `issueDirective()` records the root-cause aggregation a consumer relays to the implementer. `assertCertified()` returns the certificate covering the exact current revision for one goal and otherwise throws, which makes it the admission read an orchestrator places before `ctx.goals.complete()`. When a goal service is composed, the service also registers the same admission as a deny-only `completionGuard()` on `ctx.goals`, so `GoalService.complete()` itself rejects an uncertified completion of a measured goal; unmeasured goals complete untouched.
22	
23	Every mutation appends one durable session event carrying complete post-mutation state: `verification/standard` (author, extend), `verification/relaxation`, `verification/run`, `verification/certificate`, or `verification/directive`. Strict replay validates revisions, append-only check growth, relaxation shape, run coverage and attempt numbering, certificate coverage, and timestamp continuity, and any standard mutation invalidates the prior certificate. The session log is the only durable authority; a fresh service instance rebuilds its view from it.
24	
25	The separately published `./invariant` companion maintains an independent fold of each attached session. It rejects malformed verification changes before they enter the durable log, rejects a `goal/change` completion for a goal that a current standard measures without a covering certificate, and rejects a `verification/certificate` that no fully passing `verification/run` of the same standard revision precedes.
26	
27	## Extension points
28	
29	Policy consumers call the service verbs and fold the five events from the session log. When a projection registry is composed, a `verification` session projection serves the same state to clients: the whole current standard with its certificate and the session's directive and run counts, `null` before authorship. A certificate is a replayable record of which checks passed with what evidence and under which isolation level (`none`, `process`, `host`), so evaluation and training-data pipelines can score sessions from the log alone: per-agent tallies of certificates earned, runs attempted, directives received, and relaxations recorded derive from the events without new instrumentation. Consumers use the `Agent` interface and session events rather than importing the agent loop.
30	
31	## Model Experience
32	
33	Indirectly, through the policy consumers that relay `verification/directive` text to the implementer and admit goal completion; every event this service appends is log-only and never enters model history.
34	
35	#### KV Cache effect
36	
37	No direct invalidation; a relaying consumer owns any request-prefix changes its messages cause.
38	
39	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
40	
41	- **Admission requires the goal service** — enforcement runs inside `GoalService.complete()` through the registered completion guard when both services are composed; an assembly without `ctx.goals` keeps only the service verbs and `assertCertified()` for its own callers, and the invariant companion still rejects an uncertified completion stream wherever it is installed.
42	- **No read barrier** — this package owns durable state only; denying implementer reads of standard artifacts is filesystem-policy work in a separate plugin, and until it exists the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log.
43	- **Directive delivery is consumer work** — directives are log-only records; without a consumer that relays them as plugin-sourced user messages, the implementer never sees them.
44	- **No run executor** — the validator agent executes checks with its own tools and reports results; this package records outcomes and never spawns processes.
45	- **Trusted in-process producers** — a plugin with direct `Session` access can append counterfeit verification data. Strict replay detects malformed or inconsistent records and fails at that record; this is integrity detection, not plugin isolation.
46

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Environment runner: one registered environment as one fresh, validated session. The runner stamps the session with the environment it runs, creates the goal, authors the completion standard from the environment's checks, drives the implementer turn by turn, executes the checks through the shell executor after each turn, records the run, and completes the goal only under a certificate. The [environment-runner Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	- id: agent-default-model
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
14	  config:
15	    provider: deepseek-official
16	    model: deepseek-v4-flash
17	- id: environment-runner
18	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	  config:
20	    isolation: none
21	    maxAttempts: 2
22	    maxGoalRounds: 8
23	    checkTimeoutMs: 120000
24	    evidenceMaxChars: 2000
25	```
26	
27	| Field | Meaning |
28	|---|---|
29	| `isolation` (required) | `none`, `process`, or `host`: the isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs. A local composition that shares the filesystem between implementer and validator is `none`; a run whose checks and fixtures live on another account or host is `host`. Written into every certificate and stamp; nothing in-process can verify it. |
30	| `maxAttempts` (default `1`) | Implementer turns before the run is reported uncertified; each turn is followed by one validation. |
31	| `maxGoalRounds` (optional) | Round cap handed to goal creation; absent applies the goal service default. |
32	| `checkTimeoutMs` (optional) | Timeout override for each check command, capped by the executor; absent applies the executor default. |
33	| `evidenceMaxChars` (default `2000`) | Bound of each evidence string and of the directive detail. It must not exceed the verification service's `maxTextChars`, or `recordRun` rejects the result loudly. |
34	
35	The service requires `environments`, `agents`, `agentDefaultModel`, `goals`, `completionStandards`, `shell`, and `sessions`.
